findings.issue: The clause 'A prose-only edit to `_ui_theme.py`, a docstring or a comment, no longer owes a recapture' claims more than commit 8e382f8c did. The digest is taken over the assembled text (_surface_digest.py surface_texts(): report CSS + NUL + SCRIPT, panel UI_HTML) and nothing strips comments from it. The TOKEN_CSS string in _ui_theme.py carries CSS comments (/* ... */ at _ui_theme.py:64-119) that ship in both pages, so an edit to one still changes the digest and still owes a recapture. 'A comment' read by a changelog reader includes those, and they are most of the prose in that file. Only Python docstrings and # comments are excluded from the digest.
findings.resolution: Narrow the wording to what the page cannot see, e.g. 'a Python docstring or # comment in `_ui_theme.py`; a comment inside the CSS it emits is part of the page and still owes one'.

findings.issue: The clause 'a `scripts/ui/` part no surface claims is reported instead of passing unseen' is listed in a Changed bullet as part of this change, but 8e382f8c did not add it. The unassigned-part report existed in _output.ui_surface_digests and in loadUiSourceDigests (the `if (parsed.unassigned?.length)` lines are unchanged context in the 8e382f8c capture-screenshots.mjs diff), and was present since 9f29c519, which is in v1.0.0. Read under [Unreleased]/Changed it presents a long-standing behaviour as new.
findings.resolution: Drop the clause, or write it as unchanged ('...still reports a part no surface claims').
